name: Brightlight Desert
description: The Kingdom of Shahar was a mighty realm during the Ancient and Malrokian Ages. However, the Malrokian Curse has destroyed it. The scattered ruins, broken stone towers, and bronze dome fragments serve as remnants of its former glory. Sometimes the shifting sands uncover some of its ancient ruins with riches that attract explorers. Now, it’s a barren land with dangerous nagas, cunning rakshasas, and tribes of salamanders who share the land with the few survivors of Shahar. The human survivors split into three tribes, the Sirocchi, Zaphyrus, and Verdane. Each tribe blames the others for their land not recovering. Adorned in long robes and armed with curved blades, they became barbarian tribes, and their cultures diverged over centuries of strife. However, they still share some customs, such as honoring the dead through martial displays, and young warriors undergoing ritual combats and tests of endurance. The Sirocchi.Dwellers on high cliffs near the Ubelian Fire Pits, build fortress homes carved on cliff walls and live by stringent laws. Their warriors, sword and shield experts, braid steel chains in their hair and use white robes bearing family emblems. In grand halls, they debate law and community under their King’s gaze. They worship Tamera, but not as part of the Celestianist Church, as they deem Bauron evil. They yearn for a united Shahar and believe Tamera’s blessing will return with restored order. The Zaphyrus.These nomads wander the sands, expressing their love for freedom through their foldable silk tents and martial dances. They follow the Glorious One, believing he is the true sun’s god, and view Tamera’s faith as oppressive. Generous and cunning, they avoid violence, seeing Shahar’s fall as a lesson against greed for power. They resist restoring the kingdom, linking such ambitions to Tanares’ calamities. They advocate peace and individual freedom to appease the gods. They believe that the Verdani and Sirocchi must lay down their weapons for them all to be blessed again. The Verdani.They live in tune with the harsh desert, mastering falconry, and building homes from sandstone and plant fibers with roofs designed to collect dew. Their culture prizes the natural order, where strength reigns. They attack those they see as weak or civilized, believing that eliminating these elements will rejuvenate the desert. Their brutal view of the Nature’s Spirit faith celebrates the survival of the fittest. They are the most dangerous and brutal of the tribes, attacking travelers, merchants, and other tribes at any opportunity to prove their strength and “curb the weak”. They believe that once they kill all the Sirocchi, who dare to keep laws and a king, and all the Zaphyrus, who are cowards unwilling to let go of their traditions to embrace nature, the desert will again flourish with natural power. To make their conflict worse, water disputes are fueling animosity, with Sirocchi canals redirecting essential resources, prompting clashes. Allied to that a mysterious sickness at the oases is causing the tribes to blame one another, each trying to find a cure hidden within desert secrets and the Shahar’s ruins. The Suns’ Scroll, prophesying Shahar’s resurgence, was found by the Sirocchi, it talks about a foreigner that will uncover ancient secrets. Their king is searching for this chosen one, giving special attention to warriors and adventurers from other lands.
